To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ZO-1 has a homologue, ZO-2.
ZO-1 binds to ZO-2 through a region of sequence homology and that ZO- 1 and ZO-2 are components of the tight junction, which is the major site of cell- cell interaction in epithelial tissues.
we have isolated ZO 2 from MDCK monolayers and characterized the protein at both the molecular and tissue levels.

the identification of proteins involved in the regulation of tight junctions.

the identification and characterization of the protein complexes that mediate cell-cell adhesion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ZO-2 gene product is a ubiquitous component, in epithelial cells, of the tight junction.
ZO-1/ZO-2 proteins are the first members of a family of proteins that include ZO-1/2 proteins, p55 proteins and the product of the Drosophilal (1)discs-large-1 (dlg-1) tumor suppressor gene.
ZO-1 has been shown to be a component of the tight-junctions of MDCK cells and of other epithelial cell types, and that ZO- 1 is not a component the fascia adherents of heart myocytes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ZO-1/ZO-2 are the mammalian homologs of the dlg gene product.
ZO-1 may be involved in a number of junctions, whereas ZO-2 seems to be specific for the tight junction.
ZO-1 may have a role in both tight junctions and fascia adherens and that ZO- 2 may have a role only in tight junctions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ZO-1 family of proteins, which includes the dlg gene product of Drosophlia, is a family of tumor suppressor proteins.
ZO-1/ZO-2 is an integral part of the tight junction complex, which is a critical regulator of epithelial cell polarity and permeability.
the ZO proteins are a family of proteins that share a common domain structure, but that they have different functions and different tissue distributions.
